# Codex Sift

> An open-source model router for the OpenAI Codex CLI. It chooses a model and reasoning effort per turn while keeping the native Codex interface.

Codex Sift uses TypeSafe Jev to classify a redacted excerpt of each user turn. The YAML policy maps the result to a model and reasoning effort. Setup needs Node.js 20+, Codex CLI and a TypeSafe API key.

## Documentation

- [Homepage](https://codex-sift.vercel.app/): how routing works and installation.
- [Reduce token usage in Codex CLI](https://codex-sift.vercel.app/guides/en): model selection, context and measurement.
- [Reducir el consumo de Codex CLI](https://codex-sift.vercel.app/guides/es): guide in Spanish.
- [Manual model switching vs Codex Sift](https://codex-sift.vercel.app/compare): how to choose between workflows.
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/codex-sift): install with `npx codex-sift setup`, then run `npx codex-sift`.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/romanmeclazcke/codex-sift): code and MIT license.

## Benchmarks

- [Routing benchmark and methodology](https://codex-sift.vercel.app/benchmark): on November 26, 2026, 12 classified prompts used an estimated 48.8% less relative quota than routing every turn to forge under the repository policy.
- [Raw CLI comparison](https://github.com/romanmeclazcke/codex-sift/blob/main/reports/model-comparison.json): measured tokens, time and exact-answer scores from three short tasks under fixed, manual and Sift-selected modes.
- [Default policy](https://github.com/romanmeclazcke/codex-sift/blob/main/policy.yaml): routing rules and weights behind the quota estimate.
